title: Cleaning and Preparing Insect Specimens for DNA Extraction
author: Axel David Gonzalez Murillo
materials: A Resourced and Aid for Visualizing Topography and Structural Morphology on High Reflectance (e.g., metallicized) Exoskeletal Surfaces. Light Diffusion: Because metallic woodboring beetles (also called Jewel Beetles) often have metallicized or highly reflective external surfaces (including within foveae on the elytral surface), some structures, features, on topography on integumental surfaces may be seen more clearly by placing specimens within a fully circular or partial light-diffusing ring of opaque plastic (e.g., rings cut from of Nalgene bottle sides (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Rochester, NY, USA), or a sheet/ring of transparent (e.g., rice paper) paper that separates the exoskeletal surface from direct exposure to light from the illumination source Fig.3). Figure 3. A beetle specimen under the microscope with a light diffuser using cut, opaque plastic rings made from the sides of 200 mL Nalgene bottle (a rice-paper and foam light diffuser is visible in the background).

steps.title: Remove specimen from adhesive trap
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the specimen from the adhesive trap surface (e.g., TAD, Tanglefoot, or Pestik).

steps.title: Submerge specimen in solvent bath
steps.instruction: Place the beetle in a small glass vial or container containing Histo-Clear II (low-hazard histological clearing agent) and allow it to be completely submerged for 30 to 45 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Gently tilt the container from vertical to horizontal orientation 2 to 4 times at approximately five-minute intervals during the soak time to help dissolve adhesive.
Ensure the specimen is regularly agitated; total submersion time should generally not exceed 60 minutes.

steps.title: Transfer and mount specimen
steps.instruction: Remove the beetle from the solvent and place it in a glass or plastic petri dish lined with low-lint, absorbent lab tissue paper or wipes.

substeps.instruction: Mount the specimen on an insect pin to facilitate easier handling during subsequent cleaning.

steps.title: Perform detergent wash
steps.instruction: Dip the pinned sample into a solution of Dawn Ultra Platinum detergent and warm water (approximately 100°F / 38°C).

substeps.instruction: Avoid cold water as it hardens adhesive residue.
Avoid hot water exceeding 266°F / 130°C to prevent DNA degradation.

steps.title: Manually clean and rinse specimen
steps.instruction: Remove remaining debris and rinse the specimen.

substeps.instruction: If adhesive residue is visible, use a fine, synthetic bristle artist paintbrush to gently brush away aggregate particles and re-establish the loft of densely distributed setae.
Rinse the beetle thoroughly using a wash bottle filled with warm water.

steps.title: Dry the specimen
steps.instruction: Dry the specimen using one of the following three methods:

substeps.instruction: Natural: Leave the pinned specimen to dry at ambient lab temperature, optionally under a vented plastic cover to prevent dust accumulation.
Hairdryer: Use a dryer set to no/low heat and low airflow speed.
Compressed Air: Use a pressurized can of air (e.g., computer dust cleaner). Airflow can be modified using straws, hoses, pipette tips, or pen barrels to change the exit port diameter.

steps.title: Evaluate cleanliness
steps.instruction: Inspect the specimen for adhesive residue or environmental detritus (sand, fibers, pollen, etc.).

substeps.instruction: If the specimen is not optimally clean, repeat the detergent wash, rinsing, and drying steps.
